findings.evidence: At frame 1193 (mid-hold, the declared must-read moment for LBL-ROOT) the '1SN0S Root CA' label is a faint grey, dithered smear under the vault. legibility.json reports opacity 1.0 and plate (861,539,1116,590) for the same frame, so the measurement does not describe what is rendered. In _a (f1144) the same label is crisp on a dark plate.
findings.why: The Root CA name is a must-read label for B-05.1 and is not legible mid-beat (L-02, L-06). Regression of LEG-S1R1-10.
findings.direction: Make the nameplate solid and fully opaque for the whole hold with no dithered or noise-driven alpha, and keep it unoccluded. Make the packet measurement report the rendered opacity.

findings.evidence: During plate fades the text and plate show a grainy, speckled alpha: the check list in f0994, the CA1 and 'Earlier:' tags in f1392, 'not published here' and '1SN0S.LAB' in f2382, the check list in f2569. Several of these sit at 0.13-0.6 opacity but are still on screen at the beat boundary.
findings.why: Speckled or ghosted must-read text is not clean (L-02). This is the same symptom as the accepted LEG-S1R1-01 and CIN-S1R1-05 and regresses both.
findings.direction: Fade plates with smooth alpha, or with a position and scale exit, never dithered or hashed transparency. Do not leave half-faded plates in the frames at beat boundaries.

findings.evidence: In f0987 the 'Enroll permission granted' plate lies on top of the white request capsule and the '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' and 'Template published on this CA' plates cover the check ticks. In f2513 and f2562 the capsule is half-hidden behind the 'Template published' and 'Enroll permission' plates.
findings.why: The focal capsule is occluded by its own labels and the ticks are hidden, so the check-by-check evaluation cannot be followed. This regresses LEG-S1R1-04 and PKI-S1R1-03 (checks clear of capsule and module).
findings.direction: Move the check column fully beside the capsule and the ticks so no plate overlaps the capsule, ticks, module or nameplate.

findings.evidence: In f1924 six check plates, tightly stacked and skewed, are drawn over the gold root, intermediate and server cards, so the chain is almost completely hidden (plates 544-1070 px wide from x=544). In f1845 the first plate touches the gold root card. In f1917 the plates cover the right side of the chain.
findings.why: The checks are supposed to evaluate the chain, which is the focal subject. Covering it fails the rule that check lists stand beside the focal subject and regresses LEG-S1R1-06 and CIN-S1R1-04.
findings.direction: Place the check column clear of the chain with a stable offset and camera-facing orientation, and keep the chain visible and unoccluded throughout B-06.4 and B-06.5.

findings.evidence: In f2104 the 'Remote Desktop Authentication' plate starts about 42 px from the left edge of the 960 px image (about 84 px at 1080p), outside title-safe x>=96. legibility.json gives its plate as x=100 and x=100 appears as the left bound for many labels in many frames, which suggests the measurement is clamped.
findings.why: Title-safe fails and the measurement cannot be trusted at the edge. This regresses CIN-S1R1-08 and LEG-S1R1-09.
findings.direction: Measure unclamped projected glyph bounds and keep every label inside title-safe on every frame; do not let labels follow geometry off the safe area during camera moves.

findings.evidence: The must-read tag 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' does not appear in any of the three packet frames. legibility.json lists it only for frames 1276 and 1306, so its measured presence is at most about 1.2 s. At f1392 the CA1 and 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony' tags are at opacity 0.13. The CA=true band and the sealing by Issuing CA 1's module cannot be seen in the packet frames.
findings.why: L-06 requires a must-read label on screen for at least 1.5 s or the whole beat. A hold of about 1.2 s and an unverifiable CA=true band leave the flashback request identity unproven (AR-02). This regresses CIN-S1R1-14, LEG-S1R1-11 and PKI-S1R1-10.
findings.direction: Hold the CA-request tag for at least 1.5 s on a solid plate and show the CA=true band legibly. Add a packet frame in the middle of the tag hold so it can be checked.

findings.evidence: f1504 is a wide hero shot of the topology with no handshake action visible. In f1545 the RDP server is a tiny object at the far right with a tiny amber channel; the server and intermediate cards are about 20 px. No key pulse in the container and no handshake proof is visible. In B-06.3 the declared focal AIA indicator is a small white hexagon beside the user and the pki.1sn0s.lab kiosk is not in frame; in B-06.5 the CRL fetches are tiny amber pills.
findings.why: The proof of possession, handshake proof, AIA and CRL fetches are the point of these beats and are not readable at film scale. Regression of PKI-S1R1-06 and CIN-S1R1-06.
findings.direction: Frame the server's key container and the proof's arrival on the client large enough to read. Make the AIA indicator and the CRL fetches larger and keep the kiosk in frame.

findings.evidence: In f2697 a dark rack fills the foreground, the WEB01 label is almost invisible (about 0.3 opacity) and a white slab crosses the bottom. In f2704 a black vertical pole cuts across the '1SN0S Issuing CA 2' nameplate over the left letters and a large white slab fills the bottom, while the declared focal (CERT-CA2 / the TLS certificate) is not visible.
findings.why: Foreground geometry occludes a must-read label and the focal subject, which is the camera clipping through the set. Regression of CIN-S1R1-10 and L-06 (90% unoccluded).
findings.direction: Keep the camera out of the web server and its pole, and keep the focal certificate and the nameplate unoccluded.

findings.evidence: WEB01, portal.1sn0s.lab and WebServer-TLS plates overlap or touch edge to edge in f1504, f2145, f2187, f2944, f3030 and f3117. In f2145 a faint '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' label lies under the WEB01 plate. 1SN0S.LAB and DC01 also abut.
findings.why: Host labels and template badges must never overprint each other. Regression of CIN-S1R1-07.
findings.direction: Stagger or offset the host, site and template plates so no two overlap in any frame, and remove stale or ghosted labels behind others.

findings.evidence: CAP-S7 is fully visible at f2235 (74.5 s), but legibility.json gives appear_s 75.6 s. CAP-S9a is fully visible at f2944 (97.9 s), but the measurement gives appear_s 98.6 s. CAP-S7 is already dim at f2389 (79.6 s), though hold_end_s is 80.5 s.
findings.why: The caption timing in legibility.json does not match the rendered frames, so L-04 hold and L-05 clearance can only be checked against metadata, not pixels. Holds measured from the frames (3 s or more) still pass.
findings.direction: Derive caption times from the rendered alpha, and align the metadata and the render.

findings.evidence: The issued certificate card is a plain light-blue rectangle; no validity bar or AIA/CDP ports are visible at this scale.
findings.why: Regression of PKI-S1R1-08, which is geometry and had no hard test.
findings.direction: Make the validity bar and the small AIA/CDP ports readable at film scale.

findings.evidence: The image viewer returned no image for these frames and for all 33 strips (usage-limit removals). They were judged from legibility.json, shots.json and model-dump.json only. No legibility conclusion about them is made and no key location can be stated for them.
findings.why: Protocol requires every frame and strip to be viewed. This round's verdicts for these beats and strips are incomplete and must not be treated as cleared.
findings.direction: Re-judge these frames and all strips with a fresh instance; in particular check the private key's location in B-03.2 to B-04.2 and check PKI-S1R1-01, PKI-S1R1-02 and CIN-S1R1-11 visually.
